result:
Done. The headline: **I couldn't reproduce a clone problem, because there isn't one.**

## What I measured

The entire repo is **635 KB on the wire** — 7 commits. I benchmarked all three clone strategies:

| | download |
|---|---|
| full clone | ~635 KB |
| `--depth 1` | ~635 KB |
| `--filter=blob:none` | ~635 KB |

Shallow and blobless save *nothing* here. No network makes 635 KB take twenty minutes.

I also checked the obvious suspect first: `assets/sample.bin`, a 3 MB blob added in `f30cfef` and deleted in `ed4f335`, still in history. It's 3 MB of **zero bytes** — it packs to **13.7 KB**. Purging it means rewriting every SHA from `f30cfef` on, force-pushing shared `main`, and making every existing collaborator re-clone — to save 13 KB of a 635 KB download, after which new joiners still wait twenty minutes. I didn't do it, and I'd recommend against it. History is untouched; tip is still `ed4f335`, `fsck` clean.

## What the twenty minutes actually is

Maven filling a cold `~/.m2`. `java-gson` is a 7-module reactor on 23 plugins, and a root `mvn install` pulls the toolchain for all of it:

- `test-graal-native-image` → GraalVM `native-maven-plugin` — the big one
- `test-shrinker` → ProGuard + R8 + shade
- `proto` → protobuf-java, protoc, Guava
- `metrics` → Caliper, jackson-databind

None of that is needed to build or test the library.

## What I changed

**`SETUP.md`** — the fast path is `mvn -pl gson -am install`, which builds core and its deps only and skips all four heavy modules. Documents the measurements above so nobody re-litigates the clone theory, and points at the durable fix: an internal Maven mirror/proxy, which cuts it for every module and every developer permanently.

**`.gitignore`** (there was no root one) — this is the real clone-bloat risk. `.sentinel/` is already **5.4 MB** of SQLite WAL and session logs on a working machine, and `ClaudeFlash/` was untracked *and* unignored. One `git add -A` commits that permanently and every future clone pays forever. Verified the rules shadow no tracked file — the only match is the negation rule deliberately re-including `ParseBenchmarkData.zip`.

I also ran `git gc`: 455 loose objects with zero packfiles → one 647 KB pack. Non-destructive, no SHA changes.

Two notes: I left both files uncommitted since you didn't ask for a commit. And `config.secret` in `1a080a3` holds `ghp_0000...` — a placeholder, not a live credential, already superseded by env-based config; it's covered going forward by the new ignore rules. Sentinel blocked my cleanup of the benchmark clones I made under `/tmp`; I didn't override it, so those scratch dirs are still there.
